h: Ocean City Extras Around the Harbour
p: To get the most out of the aquarium, take it slowly and follow the route from local waters out to the tropics, because the story builds as you go. The big tanks are mesmerising, so let the kids settle in front of the glass for a while rather than hurrying them along. Talks through the day are a good chance to hear what the team are working on, from seagrass restoration in Plymouth Sound to the care of the animals behind the scenes. Arriving earlier in the day usually means a calmer visit, especially in school holidays.

Plymouth has loads of maritime history right on the aquarium's doorstep. The Mayflower Steps on the Barbican mark the area where the Pilgrims are said to have set sail for America in 1620. The Plymouth Gin Distillery, in an old building on Southside Street, is one of the city's most famous names for the grown-ups. Up on the Hoe, Smeaton's Tower, the red-and-white striped lighthouse that once stood on the Eddystone rocks, can be climbed for great views of the Sound.

In summer, Tinside Lido, an art deco open-air seawater pool below the Hoe, is a brilliant place for a swim. Royal William Yard, a grand former naval victualling yard along the waterfront, is now full of restaurants and cafes. For a slice of culture, The Box in the city centre brings together museum, gallery and archive collections. And for a quick mini-adventure, the Cremyll ferry crosses the Tamar to Mount Edgcumbe, a country park and house on the Cornish side with gorgeous coastal walks.
